## Part 01: Nvidia’s Demand Is Real. Its Financing Is Fragile.
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/nvidias-demand-insatiable-or-manufactured/
Published: 2026-08-10 · Chips · 7 min read
Dek: Google paid roughly double for Nvidia capacity while private credit financed a $35bn compute platform. The chips are scarce; the returns may be anything but.
Summary: Nvidia’s demand looks real today, but private credit, slow-to-build working compute and fast obsolescence make the revenue recurrence less secure than the backlog suggests.
The DeepStack Call (Mixed; conviction 3/5, Moderate): Bull on demand. Bear on the financing.
Call: Nvidia’s orders are real. Price its revenue as financed, not recurring.
What to do with this:
1. Discount any AI order book that leans on private credit instead of customer cash.
2. Track energized megawatts, not chips shipped: working compute is the real backlog.
3. Read the depreciation schedule before the earnings: lives that lag obsolescence flatter profit.
What would change the call:
- End customers keep absorbing capacity at market-rate financing once the power bottleneck clears.
- Nvidia’s revenue recurrence holds through the ramp, with no wave of order cancellations.
Next test: When the bottleneck clears (pending): If end demand survives market-rate financing, the financed-demand warning weakens; if recurrence falls, private-credit risk moves to the front. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p01-t01
Key numbers: $38B Apollo debt (Apollo transaction in late May, described by Michael Burry); $35B AI XPU tranche (Apollo and Blackstone first tranche; Invest In Assets, ten weeks later); 20GW Broadcom compute (Broadcom-designed capacity promised through 2028; Invest In Assets); $30B Quarterly AI orders (Broadcom orders booked in one quarter; Invest In Assets, mid-2026)

## Part 02: SpaceX Is Funding an AI Bet Before the Proof
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/spacex-after-the-ipo-exit-liquidity/
Published: 2026-08-13 · Capital Markets · 7 min read
Dek: SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO puts AI infrastructure inside a profitable Starlink shell. The capacity looks plausible; the operating proof has not reached the meter.
Summary: SpaceX’s IPO funds a credible AI buildout, but the stock is pricing future capacity before deployment, revenue quality and Starlink coverage are proven.
The DeepStack Call (Skeptical; conviction 3/5, Moderate): Ahead of the evidence
Call: SpaceX’s AI build is credible. The stock has already paid for 10 gigawatts it has not built.
What to do with this:
1. Value the AI arm on deployed gigawatts (0.4 today), not on the roughly 10 GW site plan.
2. Treat Starlink’s $4.4 billion of operating income as the collateral, not the upside.
3. Strip related-party and Anthropic-linked revenue out before calling AI demand proven.
What would change the call:
- Deployed capacity climbs toward the site plan, quarter after quarter.
- AI revenue arrives net of related-party deals and Anthropic keeps paying without the capital cycle doing the work.
Our Call takes the side “Exit liquidity”.
The strongest case against our call: Trey Henninger (2026-06-08): SpaceX at roughly 100 times trailing revenue would never qualify as a value investment, yet it is feasibly a ten-bagger: an extreme bull scenario could carry the company toward an 18 trillion dollar valuation or beyond over ten to twenty-five years. https://diyinvestingstocks.substack.com/p/spacex-ipo-hedge-against-agi
Next test: Jan 1, 2027 (pending): Quarterly deployed gigawatts will test the roughly 10 GW site plan against 0.4 GW operating now. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p02-t01
Key numbers: $75B IPO proceeds (Raised June 12 at near $1.75T valuation); 54% Peak-to-low drawdown ($225.64 to $104.83 by early August); 0.4 GW Compute deployed (Kakashii’s first-quarter reading, August 2026); $1.25B Monthly Anthropic contract (Through May 2029, as documented by Kevin Gee)

## Part 03: The Machines Will Work. The Debt Might Not.
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-debt-behind-the-machines/
Published: 2026-08-15 · Credit · 7 min read
Dek: AI demand may be real. The more dangerous question is who is financing the machines, and how quickly lenders can change their minds.
Summary: AI demand is holding up, but vendor guarantees, short-term premiums and widening credit concessions expose a fragile financing chain.
The DeepStack Call (Skeptical; conviction 4/5, High): Bearish on the credit
Call: The machines will earn. The credit stack is where this buildout breaks first.
What to do with this:
1. Watch the six-month compute premium: buyers paying double for short terms are pricing duration risk.
2. Before trusting the 21% modeled return, ask who carries depreciation when funding costs rise.
3. Price new AI debt on its concessions: wider new-issue discounts mean lenders are flinching.
What would change the call:
- Nebius’s short-term premium collapses toward long-term rates.
- H100 re-lets stay near original prices and the queued $50–60 billion of issuance clears without wider concessions.
Our Call takes the side “1999 capex plus 2008 credit”.
The strongest case against our call: Oguz Erkan (2026-08-06): Rental prices for six-year-old A100 GPUs are up more than 20 percent year-to-date, a direct read on AI model providers' willingness to pay and, by extension, end-customer demand. https://www.capitalist-letters.com/p/its-time-to-be-bullish-on-compute
Next test: Nov 10, 2026 (pending): Short-term premiums collapsing toward long-term rates would weaken the backwardation warning; persistence would make it harder to dismiss. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p03-t01
Key numbers: $500B Wall Street-arranged chip facility (Headlines, August 12, 2026); $250B Nvidia Ohio-campus guarantee (Vitaliy Katsenelson, August 6, 2026); 21% Modeled compute internal return (Market Sentiment, August 8, 2026); 6% AI paper investment-grade share (JunkBondInvestor, August 9, 2026)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/the-debt-behind-the-machines/

## Part 04: AI Spending Has Met Its First Real Bill
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-market-stops-paying-for-faith/
Published: 2026-09-04 · Capex · 9 min read
Dek: Hyperscaler capital budgets are still climbing. The market has started charging for them, rewarding cash-backed returns and punishing faith.
Summary: AI’s buildout is entering its first financing test: spending outruns cash flow, investors have separated the winners from the believers, and the next budget will expose who is right.
The DeepStack Call (Skeptical; conviction 4/5, High): Prove the return
Call: Capital intensity is not a moat. Every new AI dollar now has to out-earn its financing cost.
What to do with this:
1. Screen hyperscalers on free cash flow after capex; Alphabet’s −$6 billion quarter is the new benchmark.
2. Reward budgets that arrive with return data, not budgets that only grow.
3. Watch the labs’ growth rates: deceleration, not decline, is the trigger.
What would change the call:
- Alphabet’s larger 2027 budget lifts the stock instead of sinking it.
- Operating cash flow catches capex growth and the labs fund themselves on durable, non-circular revenue.
Our Call takes the side “The return is not there”.
The strongest case against our call: Orbis Investments (2026-08-11): Nebius, an AI-focused cloud infrastructure business with multibillion-dollar infrastructure deals with Microsoft and Meta and a $2 billion Nvidia investment, has a credible base-case pathway to over 4GW of data centre capacity by 2031 that could… https://fiscal.ai/fund-letters/orbis-investments-q2-2026-fscl_document_3VPA9VYD914
Next test: Jan 1, 2027 (pending): Alphabet discloses its higher 2027 budget; a rise in the stock revives the defense case, another fall validates the return test. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p04-t01
Key numbers: $800B Combined annual capex (Four companies, disclosed in late July); $165B Quarterly hyperscaler capex (Prof G Markets; three months, August 4); -$6B Alphabet Q2 free cash flow (Hayden Capital; Q2, first negative since 2004 IPO); $3.5T 2026–30 hyperscaler capex (Oscar Hattink via Kevin Gee; 2026–2030)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/the-market-stops-paying-for-faith/

## Part 05: OpenAI and Anthropic Are Not the Same Business
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/anthropic-grew-142-percent-openai/
Published: 2026-09-11 · AI Labs · 7 min read
Dek: OpenAI is cutting prices while Anthropic still monetizes enterprise coding. The difference matters because hyperscalers, lenders and investors have priced the pair as one AI bet.
Summary: OpenAI is losing pricing power while Anthropic still monetizes enterprise coding, exposing the risk of treating two very different labs as one AI bet.
The DeepStack Call (Mixed; conviction 3/5, Moderate): Split the trade
Call: Stop pricing OpenAI and Anthropic as one bet. One revenue line holds under pressure; the other has to be bought.
What to do with this:
1. Separate the two in any AI exposure: pricing power, not headline growth, sets the value.
2. Demand life-of-cluster margins in any prospectus, not first-year GPU economics.
3. Treat customer concentration and investor-funded revenue as the first red flags.
What would change the call:
- Anthropic is forced into an OpenAI-style price cut on coding.
- Audited losses or a DeepSeek-style price reversal erase the gap between the two businesses.
Next test: Jan 3, 2028 (pending): Return on invested capital should be visible by Romero’s deadline; failure would turn today’s extraordinary economics into a first-year illusion. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p05-t04
Key numbers: 142% Anthropic quarterly growth (Quarter on quarter, Q2 2026); 18% OpenAI quarterly growth (Quarter on quarter, Q2 2026); $20.9B OpenAI 2025 loss (Steve Eisman; 2025); $559M Anthropic adjusted income (Michael Spencer; preliminary June quarter 2026)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/anthropic-grew-142-percent-openai/

## Part 06: Power Doesn’t Depreciate. Its Premium Moves.
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/power-doesnt-depreciate/
Published: 2026-09-19 · Power · 9 min read
Dek: Electricity is the constraint, but the premium belongs to whoever can secure permission, build on time and turn a megawatt into revenue before demand catches up.
Summary: AI’s scarcity rent is shifting from chips to permitted, delivered power—but execution, politics and demand can still break the trade.
The DeepStack Call (Constructive; conviction 4/5, High): Long access, not hardware
Call: This is a power-access trade before it is a chip trade. Own the permit and the interconnect, not the loudest fleet.
What to do with this:
1. Value AI sites on connected megawatts, never on contracted ones.
2. Pay for delivery speed: Bloom’s 55-day timeline is where the premium lives.
3. Mark down GPUs parked behind late interconnections; they generate cost, not rent.
What would change the call:
- The speed-to-power premium narrows while power stays scarce.
- Recontracting fails across older fleets, or a hyperscaler cancels because compute is sufficient.
Our Call takes the side “Scarcity as a moat”.
The strongest case against our call: Michael Spencer (2026-08-26): Polling data shows roughly 70 to 75 percent of Americans oppose building large datacenters near their homes, and more than half support a national moratorium, with opposition rising since spring 2026. https://www.ai-supremacy.com/p/the-ai-backlash-is-accelerating-datacenters-2026
Next test: Dec 10, 2026 (pending): ERCOT is due to verify its first large-load batch study; the cleared list shows whether Texas weeds out speculators or rations power. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p06-t01
Key numbers: $20–25M Nebius one-to-three-year price (Michael Burry, August 12 trading post); $40–50M Nebius six-month price (Michael Burry, August 12 trading post); 23 GW NVL72 deployment need (Daniel Romero, 2027 estimate at full use); -7.9% Construction ex-data centers (Michael Burry citing Apollo, June year over year)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/power-doesnt-depreciate/
JSON: https://deepstack.ltd/api/v1/stories/power-doesnt-depreciate.json

## Part 07: The Fed Hiked. The Long End Still Climbed.
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-fed-hiked-the-long-end-kept-climbing/
Published: 2026-09-27 · Rates · 9 min read
Dek: The rate rise did not tame long yields. The bill for AI’s capital binge is arriving through bonds, deficits and the investors now setting the price of duration.
Summary: The Fed raised short rates, but long yields climbed. AI financing now sits inside a bond market priced by growth, deficits and a thinner buyer base.
The DeepStack Call (Skeptical; conviction 4/5, High): Supply sets the long end
Call: The bond market is pricing the AI bill, not a recession. The Fed cannot hike its way to a lower 10-year.
What to do with this:
1. Use a 10-year above 5% as the base case for valuing long-duration AI assets.
2. Track foreign demand, Japan first: buyers returning without a better hedge would break the supply story.
3. Circle the 2028 refinancing wave; that is when today’s rates reach AI’s borrowers.
What would change the call:
- Long yields fall while nominal growth, inflation and AI capital spending stay firm.
- Japanese and other foreign buyers return in size without a better hedge.
Our Call takes the side “A missing buyer”.
The strongest case against our call: Michael Howell (2026-09-04): US term premia remain broadly stable and have recently moved lower, with little sign they are rising relative to foreign equivalents, which undercuts the loss-of-confidence narrative for US Treasuries. https://capitalwars.substack.com/p/impossible-things
Next test: Oct 15, 2026 (pending): Treasury publishes August foreign holdings; renewed Japanese buying despite poor hedged returns would undercut the missing-buyer thesis behind the long-end selloff. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p07-t02
Key numbers: 5.18% 10-year Treasury yield (FRED, six trading days after September 16); $1.97T Federal deficit (TSCS, cumulative through August 2026); 8.25% CleanSpark note coupon (JunkBondInvestor, September 18, 2026); $2.3T Hyperscaler backlog (Apollo via DeepValue Capital, September 2026)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/the-fed-hiked-the-long-end-kept-climbing/
JSON: https://deepstack.ltd/api/v1/stories/the-fed-hiked-the-long-end-kept-climbing.json

## Part 08: AI Lenders Are Financing the End of Scarcity
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-scarcity-is-the-collateral/
Published: 2026-09-29 · Infrastructure Finance · 9 min read
Dek: The shortage of power, chips and data-center capacity supports lenders today. But every new dollar also brings the glut that can wreck their collateral.
Summary: AI capacity is scarce, but lenders are financing the supply that could erase that scarcity before hyperscaler cash flow catches up.
The DeepStack Call (Skeptical; conviction 4/5, High): Lenders are mispricing scarcity
Call: Lenders are right to finance capacity and wrong to assume it stays scarce. Scarcity is a season; debt is a contract.
What to do with this:
1. Haircut any loan secured by compute scarcity: the collateral decays as supply catches up.
2. Measure cash flow against the $2 trillion it needs, from about $600 billion today, every quarter.
3. Count the $2.7 trillion of off-balance-sheet commitments as leverage, because creditors will.
What would change the call:
- September-quarter cash flow moves visibly toward $2 trillion.
- The first Blackwell renewal holds its price without new guarantees.
Our Call takes the side “The cash has to triple”.
The strongest case against our call: Kris (2026-09-16): AWS has had more demand than supply, with customers wanting more AWS capacity for AI than could be served despite large Nvidia orders and Amazon's own Trainium chips, and Kris considers this kind of capacity-constrained spending among the best… https://www.potentialmultibaggers.com/p/best-buys-now-september-2026
Next test: Oct 20, 2026 (pending): September-quarter results test cash flow toward $2 trillion and whether maintenance costs enter accounting. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p08-t01
Key numbers: 227 bps Oracle five-year CDS (Record that week, according to Seeking Alpha); 1,146 bps CCC spread over Treasuries (September 28, 2026; FRED); $2T Hyperscaler cash-flow target (Torsten Slok’s 2030 assumption); $2.7T Off-balance-sheet commitments (Burry estimate across five hyperscalers)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/the-scarcity-is-the-collateral/

## Part 09: Habit Was the Moat. Agents Are Draining It.
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/habit-was-the-moat/
Published: 2026-10-03 · Agents · 8 min read
Dek: Meta’s Muse has inserted itself between shoppers and sellers. The first bill is coming due for businesses paid by customer inertia.
Summary: Meta’s Muse is testing whether AI shopping agents can reroute spending, squeeze weak subscriptions and expose which moats still hold.
The DeepStack Call (Mixed; conviction 3/5, Moderate): Sell habit, buy the rails
Call: Agents will drain weak consumer habits first. Back the rails (trust, records, distribution, compute), not the forgotten subscription.
What to do with this:
1. Flag businesses that live on inertia: forgotten subscriptions, commodity brands, ad-funded marketplaces.
2. Favor owners of trust, regulation, systems of record, distribution and compute.
3. Judge agent launches on retained users, transactions and fees, never on downloads.
What would change the call:
- Meta reports agent downloads without retained users, transaction volume or fees.
- The first tax season with agents shows households still paying Intuit for certainty.
Our Call takes the side “Eighteen months, or less”.
The strongest case against our call: Le Shrub (2026-09-22): Le Shrub questions whether Meta's Muse AI agent becoming popular so quickly is a big negative for OpenAI and Anthropic. https://www.shrubstack.com/p/uncomfortable-truths
Next test: Oct 28, 2026 (pending): Meta reports its September quarter; users, transaction volume and fees would show whether downloads are becoming a business. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p09-t01
Key numbers: 18% Meta stock gain (Closing prices, Financial Modeling Prep, Sep 8-Oct 2, 2026); 33% AMD stock gain (Closing prices, Financial Modeling Prep, Sep 8-Oct 2, 2026); 3% Paid consumer AI adoption (Moses Sternstein, first quarter estimate); 61%-70% Booking in AI recommendations (Oguz Erkan, September 2026)

## Part 10: The Bubble Is in the Denominator
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-bubble-is-in-the-denominator/
Published: 2026-10-07 · Markets · 9 min read
Dek: The S&P 500 looks cheaper because profits surged. But those profits depend on AI spending, chip values and debt that may be inflating the denominator while raising the discount rate.
Summary: AI spending made the market look cheaper. The harder test is whether those profits survive depreciation, weak productivity and a bond market financing the buildout.
The DeepStack Call (Skeptical; conviction 4/5, High): Cheap is conditional
Call: The market is not cheap. It is capitalizing AI earnings before anyone knows who owns them.
What to do with this:
1. Hold the 5.26% earnings yield (19.0 times earnings) against the 10-year: when the bond pays more, stocks offer no risk premium.
2. Stress-test the 29.5% earnings growth for server lives and depreciation before you pay for it.
3. Treat the $250 billion of hyperscaler bonds as competition for the savings that set the discount rate.
What would change the call:
- Used-chip values and server lives hold after scarcity fades.
- Productivity turns higher and lab revenue compounds toward the checks the infrastructure requires.
Our Call takes the side “A model, not a price”.
The strongest case against our call: David George (2026-09-30): GPUs are already running hot even while the data indicates it's still very early in mature AI adoption and utilization. https://www.a16z.news/p/state-of-markets-ii
Next test: October (pending): Anthropic filing or listing reveals audited revenue, losses and concentration, testing the $400B revenue milestone. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p10-t02
Key numbers: 19.0x S&P 500 forward multiple (FactSet, as of Oct 2, 2026); 29.5% Expected Q3 earnings growth (FactSet, as of Oct 2, 2026); $250B Hyperscaler high-grade bonds (Apollo presentation via Leyla Kunimoto, through August 2026); 5.31% 10-year Treasury yield (CNBC, closing yield on Oct 5, 2026)

## Part 11: The Backlog Is Not the Quarter
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-backlog-is-not-the-quarter/
Published: 2026-10-08 · Markets · 11 min read
Dek: Ciena carries a $10 billion order book, Microsoft's far backlog grew three times as fast as its near one, and Nvidia now waits a year to be paid. The orders will ship. DeepStack expects the profit to arrive later, and the third-quarter reports to show the gap.
Summary: AI suppliers report record order books. DeepStack reads the near book as revenue, the far book as a promise and the margin as the number that arrives last.
The DeepStack Call (Mixed; conviction 3/5, Moderate): Revenue yes, margin not yet
Call: The orders will ship. The profit comes later, and a margin that lags the ramp will be reported as a demand miss.
What to do with this:
1. Split every backlog into what is due within a year and what is not; a far book outgrowing the near one three to one is mostly forecast.
2. Credit prepaid or bring-your-own-hardware orders as revenue and the rest as options; read a residual-value guarantee as the lender's doubt.
3. Hold gross margin against the stated target before crediting the ramp: Perma-Pipe's 30% in December is the line to clear.
What would change the call:
- Microsoft's within-a-year backlog grows as fast as the beyond-a-year book on October 28.
- Nvidia's days sales outstanding give back the 14 days Eisman counted, or its terms for investment-grade customers return to 90 days.
- Perma-Pipe converts $57 million or more at a gross margin above 30% while Lumentum and Coherent report their ramps at target margin.
Our Call takes the side “Shipping is not earning”.
No case against our call has cleared DeepStack’s bar yet.
Next test: Oct 28, 2026 (pending): Microsoft reports: the share of backlog due within twelve months, 30% last quarter, and whether the near book's growth closes on the far book's 113%; at Alphabet, whether the TPU contracts inside cloud backlog get a size; at Meta, whether the $10.8 billion of restricted cash stays restricted. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p11-t01
Key numbers: $10B Ciena's backlog floor at the end of fiscal 2026 (Ciena management, as reported by Gaetano, Sep 17, 2026; supply secured through fiscal 2029); 113% Growth in Microsoft's backlog due beyond one year (Microsoft filing, as read by Michael Burry, Sep 24 to 26, 2026; the book due within a year grew 37%); 1 year Nvidia's terms for its best-rated customers (From 90 days; Steve Eisman with Ed Zitron, Sep 9, 2026); $28B Meta's residual-value guarantee on its data-center venture (Meta filing, as read by Michael Burry, Sep 24, 2026; $10.8 billion moved to restricted cash)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/the-backlog-is-not-the-quarter/
JSON: https://deepstack.ltd/api/v1/stories/the-backlog-is-not-the-quarter.json

## Part 12: The Model Is Not the Price
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-model-is-not-the-price/
Published: 2026-10-09 · Markets · 10 min read
Dek: A frontier model now lists at $4 per million input tokens, open and Chinese models carry most of the tokens on the platforms that count them, and the two labs' revenue is counted in the tens of billions. Investors agree the token is cheap. They differ on what the lab is paid for, and only a prospectus on EDGAR can settle it.
Summary: The token is cheap and getting cheaper; the labs' revenue is counted in the tens of billions, and none of it is audited on EDGAR. DeepStack reads the model's price as a four-month lease and the lab's price as a line in a filing the public has yet to read.
The DeepStack Call (Mixed; conviction 3/5, Moderate): The price has left the model
Call: A frontier model no longer commands a price per token for long. The lab still does, and only a prospectus says what that price is worth.
What to do with this:
1. Separate token volume from token dollars: OpenRouter's 57% to 67% and Vercel's 62% in September are volume; the dollar share is uncounted.
2. Date every run-rate before comparing two: Longriver's May, Romero's July and Kim's October 2 figures are not updates of one another.
3. Read the customer note before the growth rate when the prospectus lands: Silverio's quarter from two customers is the line to clear first.
What would change the call:
- A prospectus with audited revenue near the relayed run-rates, no customer above a tenth of sales and no investor-linked revenue to disclose.
- Alphabet sizes the TPU contracts with Anthropic inside them on October 28 and Cloud growth holds without them, retiring Burry's charge.
- No registration on EDGAR by October 31 while either lab cuts list prices again; the house moves toward the open-weights reading.
Our Call takes the side “The filing sets the price”.
The strongest case against our call: Market Sentiment (2026-09-17): Based on their capex sustainability model, Market Sentiment estimates that next year's ~$1.2T+ of AI capex should drive ~$2T of incremental revenue, which they say will only be a fraction of the total incremental revenue AI generates as a business… https://www.marketsentiment.co/p/the-next-great-ai-trade-is-everything
Next test: Oct 28, 2026 (pending): Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta report, and the Fed decides the same day: whether the TPU system sales inside Google Cloud's backlog get a size, and whether Cloud growth holds near the second quarter's 82% without them. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p12-t01
Key numbers: $4 vs $10 Anthropic's Opus 5.5 list price per million input tokens, against OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra (Charlie Hills, Sep 27, 2026; the frontier undercut by 60%); 57% to 67% Chinese models' share of token usage on OpenRouter by September (As counted by Michael Spencer, Oct 1, 2026; Le Shrub had 66% on Sep 22); 4 months The gap between the Chinese open models and the frontier (Torsten Slok of Apollo, citing the Epoch Capabilities Index, Jul 16, 2026); A quarter Share of Anthropic's 2025 revenue that came from two customers (Mia Silverio of Prof G Markets, Oct 5, 2026; 47% of sales ran through Amazon and Google)
Who is on each side: https://deepstack.ltd/sides/the-model-is-not-the-price/
JSON: https://deepstack.ltd/api/v1/stories/the-model-is-not-the-price.json

## Part 13: The Ratepayer Pays First
URL: https://deepstack.ltd/stories/the-ratepayer-pays-first/
Published: 2026-10-10 · Markets · 10 min read
Dek: Households in the nine jurisdictions PJM serves paid a median 11.7% more per kilowatt-hour over the year to July than the year before, against 5.6% elsewhere. Data center builders tell regulators they pay their own way. PJM's market monitor told them no state commission can shield households from the capacity price their demand sets.
Summary: Data centers pay for the wires they cause. The higher capacity price their demand sets reaches every household in PJM first. DeepStack reads both bills and names the federal price data and the December auction that will test the view.
The DeepStack Call (Mixed; conviction 3/5, Moderate): The ratepayer pays first
Call: Data centers pay for their own wires. The higher capacity price their demand sets lands first on every PJM household's bill.
What to do with this:
1. Compare medians, not states: PJM's nine rose a median 11.7% per kilowatt-hour in the year to July, against 5.6% elsewhere.
2. Separate the wire from the scarcity: pledges fund the upgrades a project triggers; the capacity price reaches every PJM bill.
3. Mark December 9: PJM's auction for 2029/2030 shows whether the price ceiling still binds.
What would change the call:
- The median gap between PJM's nine and the other 42 falls below four points in the federal data for 2026.
- A rule makes large loads bring their own capacity, and PJM's December 9 auction clears below the price ceiling.
- Texas household prices rise as fast as PJM's in the 2026 data, putting the cause in the fuel and wires both grids share.
Our Call takes the side “The bill no state can shield”.
The strongest case against our call: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (2026-02-24): Large loads inherently add volatility to load forecasts because project timelines and commitments can vary with construction, permitting approvals, grid development and data center owner decisions; revised ERCOT and PJM forecasts prepared after the… https://www.nerc.com/globalassets/our-work/assessments/nerc_ltra_2025.pdf#p2
Next test: Oct 20, 2026 (pending): The federal price data for August: whether the median twelve-month rise in household prices across PJM's nine jurisdictions stays at least four points above the median of the other 42, from 11.7% against 5.6% in July. https://deepstack.ltd/docket/#test-p13-t01
Key numbers: +11.7% Median rise in the household price per kilowatt-hour across the nine jurisdictions PJM serves, year to July 2026 (EIA-861M, first published Sep 24, 2026; DeepStack calculation; +5.6% for the other 42); +6.6% The national household price per kilowatt-hour over the same twelve months (EIA-861M, first published Sep 24, 2026; Texas +4.8%); 6,623 MW Shortfall against PJM's reliability requirement in the auction for the year from June 2027, the first since 2007 (PJM auction results as relayed by tscsw, Feb 26, 2026); $1.6B Added transmission cost on Maryland bills over 10 years (Maryland Office of People's Counsel at FERC, Jun 11, 2026)
